thread:
maya: Anyone hitting hangs in Next.js middleware when calling the redwood-inference SDK? Observed on Vercel Edge — fetch never resolves for some requests.

sam: Yep, saw this on staging too. Repro with our /middleware/embeds route. Looks like the promise just never settles, no useful stack. :confused: 

leo: Is the SDK pulling in node-fetch or fs-based auth helpers? Edge runtime uses global fetch and forbids certain node things (no dynamic require).

maya: We traced it: package exports allowed the CJS auth path to be pulled into the bundle. That code uses setTimeout-based retry and a tiny fs check, which seems to break under the Edge bundler.

arjun: Quick workaround you can try in middleware: import the edge entrypoint explicitly. Example: 
```
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, fetch: globalThis.fetch })
const r = await client.embeddings.create({ input: 'x' })
```
This avoids the node-only code paths.

talia: Also FYI — middleware runs in the Edge runtime where setTimeout is available but timers behave differently across edge providers. Our SDK's retry uses setTimeout heavily; better to switch to AbortController + retry loop that uses fetch timeouts. Example adapter: 
```
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'
const client = createClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  fetch: globalThis.fetch,
  timeoutMs: 10000 // edge adapter will use AbortController to cancel
})
```
The adapter will call fetch with signal and do backoff without relying on Node timers.

sam: Did you open an issue/PR? We should add a clear edge export conditional so Next's bundler picks the edge build instead of the node build. Something like: 
```json
"exports": {
  "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge.mjs" },
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }
}
```
That keeps compatibility and gives an explicit entry for consumers.

leo: Also watch TS types — people importing the edge entrypoint still get node types if d.ts references NodeJS types. We need a small edge.d.ts that avoids Node builtins (no fs, no Buffer). Add a note in package README about using `import ... from 'redwood-inference/edge'` in Next middleware.

maya: Filed a concise GH issue and linked a repro (sdk/issues/421). Repro steps: create Next middleware, import default SDK (not edge), call embeddings — bundle works locally but hangs on Vercel. Link: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/421>

deploy-bot: Canary deploy for patch/sdk-edge-fix started — canary id 2026-03-21-001

arjun: One extra gotcha: Next middleware runs with `edge: true` and no access to Node env helpers like `process.cwd()` in some contexts — guard uses of process.* in runtime. I saw `ReferenceError: process is not defined` on a couple of functions when bundlers tree-shook the shim.

talia: For DX, let's add a tiny sample app under examples/next-middleware-edge that demonstrates the correct import, passing global fetch, and a minimal abort-based timeout. That will reduce onboarding friction.

maya: Agreed. Plan: (1) add edge-specific build/export + edge.d.ts, (2) patch retry to use AbortController-friendly backoff, (3) add example and README note. I'll draft PRs. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — will test canary once deployed and try to reproduce the staging failure again.

leo: If anyone needs a quick script to verify bundle content, run:
```
npx npx-depcheck --json .next/server/pages/_middleware.js | grep "redwood-inference" -n
```
It helps confirm which entry got pulled into the bundle.

maya: Awesome — ping me here if you hit other edge quirks. Thanks!
